title: Uncached policy sentinel led to unbounded model fanout and cross-region thrash
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
During a traffic spike on 2026-03-09 we observed sustained cross-region reroutes and a rapid fanout of inference requests to multiple model backends. The immediate customer symptom was elevated p99 latency and timeouts for hosted API traffic in EU and NA regions; some customers reported partial responses and increased errors.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed):
A recent policy snapshot publish path missed writing a 'sentinel' flag into the regional policy cache for route suppression. The missing sentinel caused the routing mesh to treat an out-of-date policy snapshot as authoritative and trigger aggressive concurrent reroutes to model candidates across regions. That in turn invalidated several KV cache entries used for sticky routing, creating a feedback loop where requests repeatedly remapped to new backends (model fanout) until capacity stalls occurred. The core bug was a race between policy snapshot write and cache pruning that left a short-lived window where the policy was uncached but treated as valid.

Impact:
- Duration: ~42 minutes (2026-03-09 03:18 - 04:00 UTC)
- Affected surface: Hosted API routes that use smart routing + model variant fallback (approx 14% of global traffic at peak)
- Customer impact: high (time-sensitive requests saw elevated p99 and errors; some enterprise customers filed support tickets)

Detection and mitigation timeline (high level):
- 03:18 UTC: first anomalous spike in routing fanout telemetry and a rise in cross-region egress observed by routing metrics.
- 03:22 UTC: automated SLO alert triggered (p99 > 3x baseline). Ops paged on-call SRE.
- 03:28 UTC: mitigation 1 - throttle cross-region reroutes via emergency rate limiter on smart-router; reduced fanout but did not stop oscillation.
- 03:35 UTC: mitigation 2 - disabled policy hot-publish for the affected policy shard and forced a consistent snapshot reload from control-plane (stabilized sticky routing).
- 03:45 UTC: traffic returned to baseline; continued monitoring and post-incident analysis began.

Why this is different from previous routing incidents:
- No model version mismatch in payloads; model candidates themselves were compatible. The failure mode was an ephemeral cache/publish race leading to an uncached sentinel and unbounded routing fanout rather than a stale tag or explicit variant mismatch. We have seen many "fallback loops" historically; this incident is unique because the control-plane publish path silently allowed a TTL window where a snapshot was considered authoritative without the sentinel present.

Evidence and artifacts:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/routers/routing-fanout-2026-03-09
- Control plane log sample (redacted): https://drive.redwood.com/incident/ENG-621305/controlplane-logs.txt
- Playbook runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123
- Temporary mitigation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routers/pull/7890

action_items: Implement atomic sentinel write in policy publish path so a snapshot is never considered authoritative without sentinel present (owner: infra/publish-team) - estimate 5 pts
Add e2e regression test that simulates snapshot write + cache prune race and asserts routing convergence (owner: routing/tests) - estimate 3 pts
Introduce a short-circuit circuit-breaker in the smart-router to cap concurrent cross-region candidate fanout per-request (owner: routers) - estimate 5 pts
Ship dashboard panel that surfaces per-policy sentinel presence and policy-TTL drift with a pager rule (owner: observability) - estimate 2 pts
Audit recent policy releases for missing sentinel writes across shards covering Feb-Mar 2026 and backfill where needed (owner: control-plane) - estimate 3 pts
Follow-up post-deploy: run 48h canary with 100k synthetic requests exercising boundary conditions (owner: SRE/QA) - due 2026-03-28
